# Šw walks into a wind & atmospheric energy firm

Walk into any wind & atmospheric energy outfit and watch for ten minutes. You will see a very old act performed with newer props. The act has a name. It is **Šw**.

## Before the Office, the Story

**Birth from Atum.** In Pyramid Text Utterance 600, Atum stands on the primeval mound and 'sneezes Shu, spits Tefnut'.  The wordplay is precise: Shu's name resembles the word for sneeze, Tefnut's for spit.  In Coffin Texts Spells 75–80, Atum creates Shu in his mind and exhales him through the nostrils, so that Shu becomes the breath that wakes the creator from lassitude.

**Shu Lifts the Sky.** Shu and Tefnut beget Geb (earth) and Nut (sky).  But Geb and Nut are intertwined; there is no room for life between them.  Shu places himself in the interval and raises Nut above his head, arching her body into the heavens.

## The Reveal, Seat by Seat

### Wind & Atmospheric Energy

Now read the why-line with the office in mind: *He holds the sky apart from the earth and fills the space between with moving air — Egypt’s wind and breath made god.* The people doing this work did not borrow the archetype. They re-derived it — the way Šw was always going to be re-derived wherever air, wind, lions matters.

### Aviation & Aerospace

*Air and wind personified, the lift beneath the wing.* The match is not poetic license. Strip the trade to its function and the function is the myth.

### Environmental & Climate Services

Now read the why-line with the office in mind: *The atmosphere personified — the fragile, life-sustaining layer the sector exists to monitor.* The people doing this work did not borrow the archetype. They re-derived it — the way Šw was always going to be re-derived wherever air, wind, lions matters.

### Space, Astronomy & Celestial Science

*He lifted Nut from Geb and holds the sky aloft; the space between heaven and earth is his body.* Nobody in that trade worships at this temple. They just keep its hours.

### Yoga, Meditation & Holistic Wellness

*The breath of life; every breath-work practice reenacts his separation of within from without.* The match is not poetic license. Strip the trade to its function and the function is the myth.

## Not the First Rebrand

The Greeks associated Shu with Atlas, the Titan who holds up the celestial sphere — a comparison of function, not of name, since no Greek rendering of šw is attested; modern scholars repeat the comparison on the same grounds.  In Egyptian theology Shu could merge with Re (as the rays of sunlight) and with Onuris, the warrior god. The office is only the latest translation.
